chunks: Sahl, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man buys a slave girl while she is pregnant; what is permissible for him from her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Whatever is besides the private part.' I said, 'So he buys a young slave girl who has not yet menstruated and is not a virgin; does he have to observe her waiting period (istibra')?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Her matter is difficult. When it is the likes of her, suspend her and let her free her womb (i.e., observe a waiting period).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man's sexual access to a newly purchased female slave who is pregnant or young and non-virgin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a pregnant slave, sexual access is permitted except for the uterus (the 'private part' reserved for the fetus), whereas for a young non-virgin who has not yet menstruated, the ruling is stringent due to the uncertainty of lineage, necessitating istibra' (a waiting period). This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving paternity and avoiding confusion of lineage (ikhtilat al-ansab) in the context of concubinage. The term 'amruha shadid' (her matter is severe/difficult) underscores the careful scrutiny required before consummation to ensure the child's lineage is not attributed to the wrong father.
